notes: Architecture normative source; MUST; permitted_use safety_referral_trigger. No evidence_claim_ids are cited (legitimately empty per v1.2 §4.3 — architecture rules need not invent evidence claims). Per v1.2 §7.9 the trigger is any new urgent or emergency symptom appearing during a session, later the same day, or at next-day check-in; the decision is to stop the plan, re-run safety, and allow the new safety state to override phase, progression, and prior positive trends (and, per the prescription-gate dependencies V3.1 §13.4 / §22, plan confidence and readiness). Safety-state choice: §7.9 does not assign one fixed safety state; it directs a safety re-run and lets the resulting state override. The most conservative structurally appropriate closed state for a new urgent/emergency symptom is URGENT_REFERRAL (terminal; blocked_targets all; V3.1 §21), with escalation to EMERGENCY_SIGNPOSTING when the global emergency ontology is met — captured in decision_contract without inventing clinical meaning. Draft — approval_status remains pending.
